Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 4 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Anand Vijay Singh

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.
Personal counter affidavit filed today is taken on record.

2. Heard Shri S.K. Pandey (A/S 0037/2012) holding brief of Shri Anand Vijay Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner and Shri Santosh Kumar Mishra, learned Standing Counsel who appears for the respondent nos. 1 to 4.
3.
In view of the order which is being proposed to be passed, notices are not issued to the fifth respondent.

4. This Court entertained the writ petition on 22.05.2024 directing the District Inspector of Schools,
Ballia, third respondent and Finance and Account Officer, Office of District Inspector of Schools,
Ballia, fourth respondent to show cause by their own affidavit as to why petitioner's arrears of salary for the period from July, 2010 to February, 2015 calculated to the tune of Rs.1348672/- on the post Beer Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90739646/
1 of assistant clerk with interest be not paid.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Another order was passed by this Court on 30.05.2024,
followed on 08.07.2024.
5.
Today when the matter was taken up pre-recess, accommodation was sought by Shri Santosh Kumar Mishra, learned Standing Counsel for the matter being taken up post-recess.

6. Post-recess, Shri Mishra, learned Standing Counsel after giving an advance copy to the learned counsel for the writ petitioner has filed a personal counter affidavit of District Inspector of Schools,
Ballia dated 11.07.2024.

7. Shri Mishra, learned Standing Counsel has made a statement that he is well versed to the facts of the case and in view of the order which is being proposed to be passed, he does not seek for the time or to file any additional reply.
8.

Learned counsel for the writ petitioner has also made the statement that the writ petition be decided on the basis of the documents available on record as he does not intend to give reply to the personal counter affidavit filed today.
Accordingly, the writ petition is being decided at the fresh stage.

9. The case of the writ petitioner is that Aacharya J.B. Kriplani Intermediate College, Jamalpur,
District-Ballia, fifth respondent is a recognized institution and in grant-in-aid of the State and the same stands governed under the provisions of U.P. Intermediate Education Act, 1921 and the Payment of Salary Act, 1971 stands applicable.

entities.text: Aacharya J.B. Kriplani Intermediate College, Jamalpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the writ petitioner, the committee of management of the institution in question conducted selection and appointed the writ petitioner on the post of assistant clerk against the substantive vacancy and an appointment order post approval by the District Inspector of Schools, Ballia was accorded on 30.11.1985 and an appointment order was issued on 01.12.1985 and the writ petitioner assumed the charge to the post in question.

It is also the case of the writ petitioner that in pursuance of the directions contained in Writ Petition No.26307 of 2010 (Dhruv Narain Singh v. State of U.P. and others), order dated 18.05.2015, the sanctioned strength of the institution vis-a-vis, the pupil was determined and thereafter on 1st February, 2016, an office order is being stated to have been issued by the State Government and a copy whereof has been annexed as annexure-4 at page 23, reference whereof has been given in para 7 of the writ petition wherein in page 25, in para 6.1, the sanctioned strength has been determined.
According to which there is one sanctioned post of principal, four lecturers, 11 assistant teachers, 1 head clerk, two clerks, eight class-IV employees, totaling to 25.

entities.text: Writ Petition No.26307 of 2010 (Dhruv Narain Singh v. State of U.P. and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Just below the tabular chart, there happens to be a note appended thereto, according to which, it has been recited that post determination of the sanctioned strength, one post of lecturer, six post of assistant teacher, one post of clerk, and Class-IV posts are vacant.

It is also recited that one Shri Yogendra Nath Singh,
Assistant Teacher and Ranjeet Kumar Singh, lecturer, their cases have been put to investigation by C.B.C.I.D., however, so far as the writ petitioner is concerned, approval has been accorded for grant of payment of salary.

10. Learned counsel for the writ petitioner submits that in pursuance thereof also on 11.03.2016, the District Inspector of Schools, Ballia proceeded to accord a consequential order and thereafter on Beer Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90739646/
2 12.09.2021, the District Inspector of Schools, Ballia addressed a letter to the Manager/Principal of the fifth respondent, institution recommending the case of the writ petitioner for being promoted as head clerk.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
According to the writ petitioner, he has been accorded joining on 25.03.2019.
11.

The grievance of the writ petitioner is that though he is getting the current salary on the post of head clerk but so far as the areas of salary for the period from July, 2010 to February, 2015 to the tune of Rs.13,48,672/- referable to the post of assistant clerk along with interest has not been paid.
12.

As noticed above, this Court while entertaining the writ petition proceeded to pass series of orders dated 22.05.2024, 30.05.2024, 08.07.2024 requiring the personal affidavit of the District Inspector of Schools, Ballia and the Finance and Account Officer of the District Inspector of Schools,
Ballia.

13. In pursuance of the said order, a personal counter affidavit has been filed sworn by District Inspector of Schools, Ballia dated 11.07.2024 wherein in particular in para 9, it has been asserted that in compliance of the order passed by the Court in Writ Petition No. 26307 of 2010 (Dhruv Narain Singh v. State of U.P. and others) the State Government vide Government order dated 24.03.2011 determine the interim Janshakti (sanctioned strength) and a chart has been tabulated according to which, the sanction strength (interim) is for principal, one lecturer nil, assistant teacher nine post, head clerk nil, assistant clerk one post, Class-IV six post, totaling to 17 posts.

entities.text: Dhruv Narain Singh v. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In para 10 and 11, it has been asserted that the vacancy against which the writ petitioner was working as an assistant clerk w.e.f. 01.12.1985 had been declared surplus.

Further Annexure-2 at page 14,
reference whereof has been given in para 15 of the writ petition dated 28.04.2019 being an office order issued under the signature of the Secretary State Government, reference has been made in page 20 para 8.9 that so far as the case of the writ petitioner who was appointed as assistant clerk is concerned, his appointment is under investigation and, however, the approval whereof accorded without there being any proper inquiry/investigation.

14. Shri Mishra, learned Standing Counsel has also invited attention towards annexure-3 at page 23,
being a first information report lodged on 17.02.2020 purported to be under Sections 419, 420, 409,
467, 468, 471, 120-B and Section 34 of the IPC as well as 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act wherein the criminal case has been lodged and while drawing attention towards annexure-4 at page 27 being a document of the director/investigating officer, it has been asserted that inquiry is going on.

According to Shri Mishra, learned Standing Counsel, once a first information report has been lodged and inquiry is pending then the writ petitioner cannot claim any benefit whatsoever of the arrears of the salary once the vacancy against which the writ petitioner has been appointed is under cloud.

13. In rejoinder to the same, learned counsel for the writ petitioner, orally submits that from the perusal of the documents appended with the personal affidavit filed today as well as the averments contained will reveal that reference has been made in para 9 to the Government order dated 24.03.2011 determined the interim Janshakti, however, much subsequently now a final office order has been passed on 01.02.2016 determining the strength.
According to which, the writ petitioner has been made admissible to payment of salary.

He further submits that inquiry might go on, it is Beer Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90739646/
3

entities.text: Beer Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: prerogative of employer to conduct inquiry to satisfy itself but that cannot be a ground whatsoever to withhold payment of arrears of salary, particularly, when the affidavit is completely silent with regard to the fact as to whether the final determination done on 01.02.2016 as either been recalled or it is not in-existence.
He further submits that once the writ petitioner is getting current salary on the post of head clerk then there is no justification to withhold the said arrears.
14. I have the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

15. It is not in dispute that there happens to be a determination of sanctioned strength by virtue of an order dated 01.02.2016 pursuant to the directions contained in Dhruv Narain Singh (supra)
wherein in para 6.1, the final sanctioned strength has been mentioned and further entitlement of the writ petitioner has been upheld for the payment of salary on the post of assistant clerk.

The said document on a repeated inquiry being made to the learned Standing Counsel as to whether the same has been recalled or there has been any alteration, he could not give a suitable reply in this regard,
however, Shri Mishra has relied upon the interim Janshakti dated 24.03.2011.

16. Even otherwise, the Court is of the opinion that it is for the employer to take a conscious decision as to whether it would be justifiable to withhold the arrears of salary in the wake of the determination of the sanctioned strength and the existence of the said order, the fact that certain inquiry or the criminal proceedings are pending.
17.
Interestingly, the writ petitioner is getting regular salary on the post of head clerk and he is already manning the post in question.

18. Since certain issues arose and the writ petition is for a mandamus, thus, considering each and every aspect of the matter, the writ petition stands disposed of in the following manner:
(a) The writ petitioner shall prefer a comprehensive representation along with self attested copy of the writ petition and the certified copy of the order before the Principal Secretary/Additional Chief Secretary (Secondary Education) Government of U.P. at Lucknow within a period of 15 days from today.

(b) On the receipt of the said motion, the Principal Secretary/Additional Chief Secretary (Secondary Education) Government of U.P. at Lucknow shall summon the records pertaining to the claim of the writ petitioner.

(c) A notice shall be issued by the Principal Secretary/Additional Chief Secretary (Secondary Education) Government of U.P. at Lucknow to the writ petitioner and the committee of management and of-course the educational authorities for submitting their version for writing.
(d) A date shall be fixed, the parties in question would be granted opportunity to exchange their written submissions and hearing be done by fixing dates.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (e) Final orders be passed within a period of four months from the date of the submission of the certified copy of the order.

19. In case, the Principal Secretary/Additional Chief Secretary (Secondary Education) Government of U.P. at Lucknow is of the opinion that some other authority empowered and competent to take decision is to accord consideration then the papers be transmitted to it and the procedure as envisaged shall be adhered to and orders be passed strictly in accordance with law after hearing the parties.

20. The authority who shall pass orders shall consider the following aspects:
(i) The issue with regard to the sanctioned strength of the students and the pupil as claimed by the writ petitioner to have been determined on 01.02.2016.
(ii) Import and the impact of the order dated 01.02.2016 determining the strength.
(iii) The effect in relation to the claim that the writ petitioner has been promoted from the post of assistant clerk to head clerk and he is getting regular salary.
(iv) Import and the impact of the interim Janshakti as well as the final Janshakti.
(v) Effect of pendency of criminal case or investigation while withholding the arrears despite the fact that the applicant claims that approval of his appointment has been accorded.
(vi) Any other incidental or ancillary issue.
21. With the aforesaid observations, the writ petition stands disposed of.

Order Date :- 15.7.2024 A. Prajapati  Beer Bahadur Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90739646/
